title: Add replayable, a cache for functions that produce iterables
description: Adds `replayable` to `more_itertools/more.py`: a decorator, usable as `@replayable` or `@replayable(maxsize=...)`, for a function that returns an iterable, typically a generator function that is slow to run. The first call with some arguments calls the function and returns an iterator over its items while recording them; once that iterator has been exhausted, later calls with equal arguments replay the recorded items and do not call the function at all. Only a run that reaches the end is recorded: if the function raises, or the iterator is closed or discarded early, nothing is kept and the next call runs the function again. Arguments match by equality, and a keyword argument never matches a positional one. A call whose arguments cannot be hashed goes straight to the function and is not recorded. At most `maxsize` results (default 128) are kept, dropping the least recently used one to make room; `maxsize=None` keeps everything, and zero or a negative `maxsize` keeps nothing, as with `functools.lru_cache`. The decorated function gets `cache_info()`, which returns `(hits, misses, currsize)`, and `cache_clear()`, which drops every recorded result and resets the counts; a run that is still going when the cache is cleared records nothing when it finishes. Includes a type stub and tests.

defects.summary: func is called before the cache is checked, so every replay still runs a function that does its work when called.
The run is recorded in a finally block, so a run that raises or is closed early is stored as if it were complete and later calls replay the partial result.
OrderedDict.popitem() drops the newest entry, so once the cache is full the result just stored is thrown away instead of the least recently used one.
cache_clear() resets the generation to 0 instead of advancing it, so a run that was under way when the cache was cleared still records its result.
Keyword arguments are appended to the key without a marker, so f(1, ('b', 2)) and f(1, b=2) share a recording.

ceiling.summary: replay() treats an empty recording as no recording, but record() stores a run that produced nothing as an empty list, so a function whose run yields no items is called again on every call instead of being replayed.

decoys.anchor:
if maxsize is not None and maxsize < 0:
        maxsize = 0
decoys.why: A negative maxsize keeping nothing is the documented contract, the same as functools.lru_cache.
Any failure of hash() means the call cannot be recorded, and such calls are documented to go straight to func; the try covers hash() only, never func.
